claim: p53 is mutated in approximately 50% of all types of human cancers.
source: p53 executes its tumor suppressive function mainly by inducing the expression of a large number of genes involved in cell cycle control, senescence, apoptosis, ferroptosis, autophagy, and metabolism (Jiang et al., 2015; Kruiswijk et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Levine and Oren, 2009).

claim: p53 functions are impaired through various mechanisms in human cancers that do not have p53 mutations.
source: Tumorigenesis is highly associated with inactivation of the tumor suppressor p53, as it is mutated in ~50% of all types of human cancers, and its functions are impaired through various mechanisms in the rest of human cancers (Levine and Oren, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: p53 executes its tumor suppressive function mainly by inducing the expression of a large number of genes involved in cell cycle control, senescence, apoptosis, ferroptosis, autophagy, and metabolism.
source: p53 executes its tumor suppressive function mainly by inducing the expression of a large number of genes involved in cell cycle control, senescence, apoptosis, ferroptosis, autophagy, and metabolism (Jiang et al., 2015; Kruiswijk et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: MDM2 is an oncoprotein encoded by a p53 transcriptional target gene.
source: One key monitor of p53 is MDM2 (HDM2 in human), an oncoprotein encoded by a p53 transcriptional target gene that is amplified or overexpressed in several human tumors (Fakharzadeh et al., 1991; Momand et al., 1992; Oliner et al., 1992, 1993; Wu et al., 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: MDM2 is amplified or overexpressed in several human tumors.
source: One key monitor of p53 is MDM2 (HDM2 in human), an oncoprotein encoded by a p53 transcriptional target gene that is amplified or overexpressed in several human tumors (Fakharzadeh et al., 1991; Momand et al., 1992; Oliner et al., 1992, 1993; Wu et al., 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: MDM2 inhibits p53 activity primarily by binding to and concealing the N-terminal transcriptional activation (TA) domain of p53.
source: MDM2 inhibits p53 activity primarily by binding to and concealing the N-terminal transcriptional activation (TA) domain of p53 (Oliner et al., 1993) and by mediating its poly-ubiquitination and proteolysis (Fuchs et al., 1998; Haupt et al., 1997; Kubbutat et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: MDM2 inhibits p53 activity by mediating its poly-ubiquitination and proteolysis.
source: MDM2 inhibits p53 activity primarily by binding to and concealing the N-terminal transcriptional activation (TA) domain of p53 (Oliner et al., 1993) and by mediating its poly-ubiquitination and proteolysis (Fuchs et al., 1998; Haupt et al., 1997; Kubbutat et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Disruption of the TP53 gene completely rescues the lethal phenotype of Mdm2 knockout mice.
source: Genetically, disruption of the TP53 gene completely rescues the lethal phenotype of Mdm2 knockout mice (Jones et al., 1995; Montes de Oca Luna et al., 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The ARF tumor suppressor directly associates with MDM2 and inhibits MDM2-mediated p53 ubiquitination and degradation upon oncogenic stress.
source: The ARF tumor suppressor directly associates with MDM2 and inhibits MDM2-mediated p53 ubiquitination and degradation upon oncogenic stress (Palmero et al., 1998; Zhang et al., 1998; Zindy et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Several ribosomal proteins boost p53 activation by untying the MDM2-p53 loop in response to ribosomal or nucleolar stress.
source: Also, several ribosomal proteins boost p53 activation by untying the MDM2-p53 loop in response to ribosomal or nucleolar stress (Zhang and Lu, 2009; Zhou et al., 2012, 2015a).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: MDMX can enhance MDM2-mediated p53 proteasomal degradation by binding to MDM2.
source: MDMX (also called MDM4), the MDM2 homologue, can enhance MDM2-mediated p53 proteasomal degradation by binding to MDM2, besides directly interacting with p53 and repressing its activity (Shvarts et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: MDMX directly interacts with p53 and represses its activity.
source: MDMX (also called MDM4), the MDM2 homologue, can enhance MDM2-mediated p53 proteasomal degradation by binding to MDM2, besides directly interacting with p53 and repressing its activity (Shvarts et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: High expression of MDM2 and MDMX in several cancers, such as breast cancer and melanoma, is often considered as the reason why these cancers sustain wild type p53.
source: High expression of MDM2 and MDMX in several cancers, such as breast cancer and melanoma, is often considered as the reason why these cancers sustain wild type (wt) p53 (Wade et al., 2013), but this could only account for a portion of wt p53-harboring cancers.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: NGFR is a 75 kD single-transmembrane protein without kinase activity.
source: NGFR is a 75 kD single-transmembrane protein without kinase activity and widely expressed in the central and peripheral nervous system (Barker, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: NGFR is widely expressed in the central and peripheral nervous system.
source: NGFR is a 75 kD single-transmembrane protein without kinase activity and widely expressed in the central and peripheral nervous system (Barker, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: NGFR is involved in a multitude of processes during neurogenesis, such as neural cell death, neuronal differentiation, neurite growth, and synaptic plasticity.
source: Often partnering with other receptors, such as TrkA, it is involved in a multitude of processes during neurogenesis, such as neural cell death, neuronal differentiation, neurite growth, and synaptic plasticity (Barker, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The NGF-NGFR cascade activates NF-κB, leading to inhibition of apoptosis.
source: Also, the NGF-NGFR cascade activates NF-κB, leading to inhibition of apoptosis (Carter et al., 1996) and increased survival of schwannoma (Ahmad et al., 2014; Gentry et al., 2000) and breast cancer cells (Descamps et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The NGF-NGFR cascade leads to increased survival of schwannoma cells.
source: Also, the NGF-NGFR cascade activates NF-κB, leading to inhibition of apoptosis (Carter et al., 1996) and increased survival of schwannoma (Ahmad et al., 2014; Gentry et al., 2000) and breast cancer cells (Descamps et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The NGF-NGFR cascade leads to increased survival of breast cancer cells.
source: Also, the NGF-NGFR cascade activates NF-κB, leading to inhibition of apoptosis (Carter et al., 1996) and increased survival of schwannoma (Ahmad et al., 2014; Gentry et al., 2000) and breast cancer cells (Descamps et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Overexpression of NGFR observed in many metastatic cancers promotes tumor migration and invasion.
source: In addition, overexpression of NGFR observed in many metastatic cancers promotes tumor migration and invasion (Boiko et al., 2010; Civenni et al., 2011; Johnston et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: In prostate and bladder cancers, NGFR appears to suppress tumor growth and/or metastasis.
source: But, in prostate and bladder cancers, NGFR appears to suppress tumor growth and/or metastasis (Krygier and Djakiew, 2002; Tabassum et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: p53 binds to the NGFR promoter and induces its expression in cancer cells.
source: These studies together with our initial findings that p53 binds to the NGFR promoter and induces its expression in cancer cells motivated us to further explore the functional interplay between NGFR and p53, and its role in cancer development.
evidence: This claim is stated as an initial finding by the authors.

claim: NGFR inactivates p53 by directly binding to its central DNA-binding domain and preventing its association with its target promoters.
source: As detailed below, we surprisingly found that NGFR inactivates p53 by directly binding to its central DNA-binding domain and preventing its association with its target promoters and by enhancing its MDM2-mediated ubiquitination and proteolysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: NGFR inactivates p53 by enhancing its MDM2-mediated ubiquitination and proteolysis.
source: As detailed below, we surprisingly found that NGFR inactivates p53 by directly binding to its central DNA-binding domain and preventing its association with its target promoters and by enhancing its MDM2-mediated ubiquitination and proteolysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: NGFR's function in inactivating p53 is ligand-independent because it occurred in the nucleus and without ligand treatment of cancer cells.
source: This function is ligand-independent because it occurred in the nucleus and without ligand treatment of cancer cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations presented in the manuscript.

claim: Down regulation of NGFR induced p53-dependent apoptosis and cell growth arrest.
source: Biologically, cancer cells hijack the negative feedback regulation of p53 by NGFR to their growth advantage, as down regulation of NGFR induced p53-dependent apoptosis and cell growth arrest as well as suppressed tumor growth.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Down regulation of NGFR suppressed tumor growth.
source: Biologically, cancer cells hijack the negative feedback regulation of p53 by NGFR to their growth advantage, as down regulation of NGFR induced p53-dependent apoptosis and cell growth arrest as well as suppressed tumor growth.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: NGFR was found to be highly expressed in 68.75% (33/48) of human gliomas examined.
source: Furthermore, NGFR was found to be highly expressed in 68.75% (33/48) of human gliomas examined.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from human tissue samples.

claim: NGFR is amplified in breast cancers that harbor wild type TP53 based on the TCGA database.
source: Consistently, NGFR is amplified in breast cancers that harbor wt TP53 based on the TCGA database (Cerami et al., 2012; Gao et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of the TCGA database.

claim: NGFR mRNA expression is elevated by Inauhzin in HCT116 p53+/+ cells.
source: HCT116 p53+/+ (A) H460 (B) and HepG2 (C) cells were treated with Inauhzin, Doxorubicin or 5-Fluorouracil for 15 h, and NGFR expression was determined by q-PCR (Mean ± SEM, n = 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by q-PCR data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: NGFR mRNA expression is elevated by Doxorubicin in HCT116 p53+/+ cells.
source: HCT116 p53+/+ (A) H460 (B) and HepG2 (C) cells were treated with Inauhzin, Doxorubicin or 5-Fluorouracil for 15 h, and NGFR expression was determined by q-PCR (Mean ± SEM, n = 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by q-PCR data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: NGFR mRNA expression is elevated by 5-Fluorouracil in HCT116 p53+/+ cells.
source: HCT116 p53+/+ (A) H460 (B) and HepG2 (C) cells were treated with Inauhzin, Doxorubicin or 5-Fluorouracil for 15 h, and NGFR expression was determined by q-PCR (Mean ± SEM, n = 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by q-PCR data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: NGFR protein expression is elevated by Doxorubicin in HCT116 p53+/+ cells but not in HCT116 p53-/- cells.
source: HCT116 p53+/+ and HCT116 p53-/- cells were treated with Doxorubicin or 5-Fluorouracil for 15 hr followed by IB using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: NGFR protein expression is elevated by 5-Fluorouracil in HCT116 p53+/+ cells but not in HCT116 p53-/- cells.
source: HCT116 p53+/+ and HCT116 p53-/- cells were treated with Doxorubicin or 5-Fluorouracil for 15 hr followed by IB using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: NGFR protein expression is elevated by Doxorubicin in HepG2 cells but not in PCL/PRF/5 cells.
source: HepG2 and PLC/PRF/5 cells were treated with Doxorubicin or 5-Fluorouracil for 15 hr followed by IB using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Ectopic wild-type p53 induces NGFR mRNA expression in p53-deficient HCT116 p53-/- cells.
source: HCT116 p53-/- (F) and H1299 (G) cells were transfected with wild-type or mutant p53 for 30 hr and NGFR expression was determined by q-PCR (Mean ± SEM, n = 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by q-PCR data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Ectopic mutant p53 does not induce NGFR mRNA expression in p53-deficient HCT116 p53-/- cells.
source: HCT116 p53-/- (F) and H1299 (G) cells were transfected with wild-type or mutant p53 for 30 hr and NGFR expression was determined by q-PCR (Mean ± SEM, n = 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by q-PCR data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Knockdown of p53 markedly reduces NGFR mRNA level in HCT116 p53+/+ cells.
source: HCT116 p53+/+ (H) and H460 (I) cells were transfected with p53 or control siRNA for 72 hr, and Doxorubicin or 5-Fluorouracil was supplemented 15 hr before the cells were harvested for q-PCR (Mean ± SEM, n = 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by q-PCR data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: p53 induces luciferase activity through RE1 in H1299 cells.
source: Luciferase assay was performed using H1299 and U2OS cells as described in Materials and methods (Mean ± SEM, n = 3 biological replicates).
evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 1K.

claim: p53 induces luciferase activity through RE1 in U2OS cells.
source: Luciferase assay was performed using H1299 and U2OS cells as described in Materials and methods (Mean ± SEM, n = 3 biological replicates).
evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 1L.

claim: Endogenous p53 specifically associates with the RE1-containing NGFR promoter in HCT116 p53+/+ cells.
source: HCT116 p53+/+ cells were treated with or without Doxorubicin for 15 hr followed by ChIP assay using anti-p53 or mouse IgG.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP assay data shown in Figure 1M.

claim: The association of p53 with the RE1-containing NGFR promoter is enhanced by Doxorubicin treatment in HCT116 p53+/+ cells.
source: HCT116 p53+/+ cells were treated with or without Doxorubicin for 15 hr followed by ChIP assay using anti-p53 or mouse IgG.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP assay data shown in Figure 1M and N.

claim: Knockdown of NGFR elicits significant apoptosis of H460 cells.
source: Cells were transfected with NGFR or control siRNA for 72 to 96 hr, and Doxorubicin was supplemented 15 hr before the cells were harvested for flow cytometry analyses.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: Knockdown of NGFR elicits significant apoptosis of HCT116 p53+/+ cells.
source: Cells were transfected with NGFR or control siRNA for 72 to 96 hr, and Doxorubicin was supplemented 15 hr before the cells were harvested for flow cytometry analyses.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: Knockdown of NGFR reduces cell viability of H460 cells during 4-day culture.
source: H460 (E) and HCT116 p53+/+ (F) cells were transfected with NGFR or control siRNA and seeded in 96-well plate the next day (Day 1). Cell viability was evaluated every 24 hr (Mean ± SEM, n = 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell viability assay data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Knockdown of NGFR reduces cell viability of HCT116 p53+/+ cells during 4-day culture.
source: H460 (E) and HCT116 p53+/+ (F) cells were transfected with NGFR or control siRNA and seeded in 96-well plate the next day (Day 1). Cell viability was evaluated every 24 hr (Mean ± SEM, n = 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell viability assay data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: NGFR ablation more dramatically represses the colony formation of H460 cells than that of H1299 cells.
source: H460 and H1299 cells were transfected with NGFR or control siRNA and seeded in 10-cm plates the next day. Colonies were fixed by methonal and stained with crystal violet solution (left panel). Quantification of colonies is shown in the right panel (Mean ± SEM, n = 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by colony formation assay data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: NGFR is more highly expressed in human glioma tissues compared to adjacent tissues.
source: IB analyses of human glioma and the adjacent noncancerous tissues (left panel). Quantification of NGFR expression (right panel) (Mean ± SEM, n = 48, p*<0.01).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Ectopic NGFR markedly reduces p53 level induced by Doxorubicin in H460 cells.
source: H460 cells were transfected with NGFR for 30 hr and treated with Doxorubicin or 5-Fluorouracil for 15 hr before harvested for IB using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Ectopic NGFR markedly reduces p53 level induced by 5-Fluorouracil in H460 cells.
source: H460 cells were transfected with NGFR for 30 hr and treated with Doxorubicin or 5-Fluorouracil for 15 hr before harvested for IB using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Knockdown of NGFR strikingly elevates the level of endogenous p53 in H460 cells.
source: A panel of cancer cell lines were transfected with NGFR or control siRNA followed by IB using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Knockdown of NGFR strikingly elevates the level of p53 target gene p21 in H460 cells.
source: A panel of cancer cell lines were transfected with NGFR or control siRNA followed by IB using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Knockdown of NGFR strikingly elevates the level of p53 target gene PUMA in H460 cells.
source: A panel of cancer cell lines were transfected with NGFR or control siRNA followed by IB using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Knockdown of NGFR leads to the global expression of a group of known p53 target genes in H460 cells.
source: H460 cells were transfected with NGFR or control siRNA followed by RNA-sequencing analyses. Genes with over 1.5-fold increase in expression were shown (Three biological replicates were used for p value, p<0.05.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Ablation of NGFR prolongs p53's half-life in H460 cells.
source: H460 cells transfected with NGFR or control siRNA for 72 hr were treated with 100 µg/ml of CHX and harvested at the time points as indicated. IB was performed using antibodies as indicated (upper panel) and quantification of p53/β-actin ratio is shown in the lower panel.
evidence: This claim is supported by cycloheximide chase assay data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Ectopic NGFR enhances MDM2-mediated p53 ubiquitination in a dose-dependent manner in H1299 cells.
source: H1299 cells were transfected with combinations of plasmids encoding p53, HA-MDM2, Myc-NGFR or His-Ub and treated with MG132 6 hr before harvested for in vivo ubiquitination assay. Bound proteins and inputs were detected by IB using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo ubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: NGFR enhances MDM2-mediated p53 proteasomal degradation in H1299 cells.
source: H1299 cells were transfected with combinations of plasmids encoding p53, HA-MDM2 or RFP-NGFR followed by IB using antibodies as indicated. MG132 was supplemented to the medium for 6 hr.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: MDM2-mediated p53 proteasomal degradation by NGFR is abolished by the proteasome inhibitor MG132.
source: H1299 cells were transfected with combinations of plasmids encoding p53, HA-MDM2 or RFP-NGFR followed by IB using antibodies as indicated. MG132 was supplemented to the medium for 6 hr.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Without MDM2, NGFR is unable to alter p53 protein level in cells.
source: MEF p53-/-;Mdm2-/- cells were transfected with combinations of plasmids encoding Myc-NGFR, HA-MDM2 or p53 followed by IB using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: NGFR interacts with p53 in the absence of MDM2 in MEF p53-/-;Mdm2-/- cells.
source: MEF p53-/-;Mdm2-/- cells were transfected with plasmids encoding Myc-NGFR or p53 followed by co-IP-IB assays using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP-IB data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: NGFR represses p53-induced luciferase activity independently of MDM2 in MEF p53-/-;Mdm2-/- cells.
source: MEF p53-/-;Mdm2-/- cells were transfected with plasmids as indicated in the figure and luciferase assay was performed as described in Materials and methods (Mean ± SEM, n = 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: NGFR inhibits p53-induced target gene expression independently of MDM2 in MEF p53-/-;Mdm2-/- cells.
source: MEF p53-/-;Mdm2-/- cells were transfected with plasmids as indicated in the figure followed by q-PCR analysis (Mean ± SD, n = 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by q-PCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: NGFR impedes p53 association with the p21 promoter in H1299 cells.
source: Cells were transfected with plasmids as indicated and treated with MG132 for 6 hr before harvested for ChIP-PCR analyses.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-PCR data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: NGFR impedes p53 association with the p21 and Bax promoters independently of MDM2 in MEF p53-/-;Mdm2-/- cells.
source: MEF p53-/-;Mdm2-/- cells were transfected with plasmids as indicated followed by ChIP-PCR analyses.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-PCR data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Ectopic NGFR binds to ectopic MDM2 in H1299 cells.
source: H1299 cells were transfected with plasmids encoding Myc-NGFR, Flag-MDM2 or HA-MDM2 followed by co-IP-IB assays using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP-IB data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: NGFR binds to the C-terminal aa 284–491 fragment of MDM2 in H1299 cells.
source: H1299 cells were transfected with the plasmid encoding V5-tagged MDM2 fragment, aa 1–150, aa 1–301 or aa 284–491, along with the Myc-NGFR-encoded plasmid. Co-IP-IB assays were performed using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP-IB data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: NGFR binds to the C-terminal aa 284–491 fragment of MDM2 in vitro.
source: The prokaryotic expressed GST-tagged MDM2 fragment, aa 1–150, aa 1–301 or aa 284–491, or GST protein alone was incubated with cell lysates overexpressing Myc-NGFR. Bound proteins were detected by IB using anti-NGFR or coomassie staining.
evidence: This claim is supported by GST-pull down assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: MDM2 interacts with the N-terminal extracellular and transmembrane domain of NGFR in H1299 cells.
source: H1299 cells were transfected with the plasmid encoding Myc-tagged NGFR fragment, aa 1–272 or aa 273–427, along with the Flag-MDM2-encoded plasmid. Co-IP-IB assays were performed using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP-IB data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Endogenous NGFR and MDM2 interact in human neuroblastoma SK-N-SH cells.
source: Cells treated with Doxorubicin for 12 hr and MG132 for 6 hr were harvested for co-IP-IB assays using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP-IB data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Full-length NGFR is present in both cytoplasm and nucleus of H460 cells stably expressing NGFR.
source: NGFR-stably expressed H460 (A), SK-MEL-147 (B) and HCT116 p53+/+ cells (C) were fractionated into nuclear and cytoplasmic/membrane fractions which were subsequently subjected to IB using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell fractionation and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Full-length NGFR is present in both cytoplasm and nucleus of SK-MEL-147 cells.
source: NGFR-stably expressed H460 (A), SK-MEL-147 (B) and HCT116 p53+/+ cells (C) were fractionated into nuclear and cytoplasmic/membrane fractions which were subsequently subjected to IB using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell fractionation and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Full-length NGFR is present in both cytoplasm and nucleus of HCT116 p53+/+ cells.
source: NGFR-stably expressed H460 (A), SK-MEL-147 (B) and HCT116 p53+/+ cells (C) were fractionated into nuclear and cytoplasmic/membrane fractions which were subsequently subjected to IB using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell fractionation and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: NGFR is present in all cellular compartments of SK-MEL-147 cells, albeit with less intensity in the nucleus than in the cytoplasm.
source: SK-MEL-147 cells were treated with or without Dox for 20 hr and fixed in −20°C for overnight. The fixed cells were subjected to immunostaining using antibodies as indicated. The images were acquired by a confocal microscope.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The nuclear and cytoplasmic levels of NGFR increase upon Doxorubicin treatment in SK-MEL-147 cells.
source: SK-MEL-147 cells were treated with or without Dox for 20 hr and fixed in −20°C for overnight. The fixed cells were subjected to immunostaining using antibodies as indicated. The images were acquired by a confocal microscope.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: NGFR is co-immunoprecipitated with MDM2 from the nuclear extracts of NGFR-stably expressed H460 cells.
source: Nuclear fractions from NGFR-stably expressed H460 (I) and SK-MEL-147 cells (J,K) were subjected to co-IP-IB assays using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP-IB data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: NGFR is co-immunoprecipitated with MDM2 from the nuclear extracts of SK-MEL-147 cells.
source: Nuclear fractions from NGFR-stably expressed H460 (I) and SK-MEL-147 cells (J,K) were subjected to co-IP-IB assays using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP-IB data shown in Figure 5J.

claim: NGFR and p53 co-immunoprecipitate with each other in reciprocal co-IP-IB assays in H1299 cells.
source: H1299 cells were transfected with plasmids encoding Myc-NGFR, Flag-p53 or p53 followed by co-IP-IB assays using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP-IB data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: NGFR binds to the central DNA-binding domain of p53 (aa 101–300) in H1299 cells.
source: H1299 cells were transfected with the plasmid encoding flag-tagged p53 fragment, aa 1–300, aa 101–300, aa 101–393 or aa 301–393, along with the Myc-NGFR-encoded plasmid. Co-IP-IB assays were performed using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP-IB data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: NGFR specifically binds to the full-length p53 and its central DNA-binding domain (aa 101–300) in vitro.
source: The prokaryotic expressed GST-tagged full-length p53 or p53 fragment, aa 1–73, aa 100–290 or aa 291–393, or GST protein alone was incubated with cell lysates overexpressing Myc-NGFR. Bound proteins were detected by IB using anti-NGFR or coomassie staining.
evidence: This claim is supported by GST-pull down assay data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: p53 binds to the N-terminal region of NGFR (aa 1–272) in H1299 cells.
source: H1299 cells were transfected with the plasmid encoding Myc-tagged NGFR fragment, aa 1–272 or aa 273–427, along with the V5-p53-encoded plasmid. Co-IP-IB assays were performed using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP-IB data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: NGFR binds to p53 in the nucleus of NGFR-stably expressed H460 cells.
source: Nuclear fractions from NGFR-stably expressed H460 (I) and SK-MEL-147 cells (J,K) were subjected to co-IP-IB assays using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP-IB data shown in Figure 5I and K.

claim: NGFR binds to p53 in the nucleus of SK-MEL-147 cells.
source: Nuclear fractions from NGFR-stably expressed H460 (I) and SK-MEL-147 cells (J,K) were subjected to co-IP-IB assays using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP-IB data shown in Figure 5J and K.

claim: Both Doxorubicin and Cisplatin induce p53 and its target PUMA or p21 more apparently when H460 cells are transfected with NGFR siRNA compared to control siRNA.
source: Cells were transfected with NGFR or control siRNA for 72 hr and Cisplatin (A) or Doxorubicin (B) was supplemented in the medium 12 hr before the cells were harvested for IB using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: Both Doxorubicin and Cisplatin induce p53 and its target p21 more apparently when SK-N-SH cells are transfected with NGFR siRNA compared to control siRNA.
source: The same experiments as shown in (A,B) were performed except that the SK-N-SH cell line was used instead.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 7C and D.

claim: The IC50 of Cisplatin in NGFR siRNA-transfected H460 cells is 2.2-fold less than that in control siRNA-transfected H460 cells.
source: Cells were transfected with NGFR or control siRNA and seeded in 96-well plates the next day. Cisplatin was supplemented 48 hr before cell viability was determined using CCK-8 as described in Materials and methods.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell viability assay data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The IC50 of Cisplatin in NGFR siRNA-transfected HCT116 p53+/+ cells drops by 1.6 folds compared to control siRNA-transfected cells.
source: The same experiments described in (E,F) were performed except for using different cell lines.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell viability assay data shown in Figure 7G.

claim: No significant difference in cell viability is observed when p53-null H1299 cells are treated with Cisplatin after NGFR knockdown.
source: Cells were transfected with NGFR or control siRNA and seeded in 96-well plates the next day. Cisplatin was supplemented 48 hr before cell viability was determined using CCK-8 as described in Materials and methods.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell viability assay data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: No significant difference in cell viability is observed when HCT116 p53-/- cells are treated with Cisplatin after NGFR knockdown.

claim: The expression of p53 and its target genes p21, PUMA, and MDM2 is induced by knocking down NGFR using shRNA-expressing lentiviruses in H460 cells.
source: H460 cells were transduced with lentivirus expressing NGFR or control shRNA for 72 hr followed by IB using antibodies as indicated.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: H460 cells with deficient NGFR grow slowly.
source: H460 cells stably expressing NGFR or control shRNA were seeded in 96-well plates and cell viability was evaluated every 24 hr (Mean ± SEM, n = 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell viability assay data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: H460 cells with deficient NGFR form fewer colonies.
source: H460 cells stably expressing NGFR or control shRNA were seeded on 10-cm plates and colonies were fixed by methonal and stained with crystal violet solution (upper panel). Quantification of colonies is shown in the lower panel.
evidence: This claim is supported by colony formation assay data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Xenograft tumors derived from NGFR-shRNA H460 cells grow remarkably slower than those from control-shRNA H460 cells in SCID mice.
source: H460 cells stably expressing NGFR shRNA reveal less xenograft tumor volume in average (Mean ± SEM, n = 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by xenograft tumor growth data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: The average tumor weight from control H460 cells is approximately ten-fold heavier than that from NGFR-shRNA H460 cells by the end of the xenograft experiment.
source: H460 cells stably expressing NGFR shRNA reveal less xenograft tumor weight in average (Mean ± SEM, n = 6). Six pairs of tumors were used for p value, p*<0.01.
evidence: This claim is supported by xenograft tumor weight data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: The expression of p21, PUMA, and MDM2 is significantly elevated in response to NGFR depletion in the xenograft tumors.
source: The p53 pathway is activated by NGFR knockdown in the xenograft tumors. The expression of p21, PUMA and MDM2 was determined by q-PCR (Mean ± SEM, n = 3). Three pairs of tumors were used for p value, p*<0.01.
evidence: This claim is supported by q-PCR data shown in Figure 8G.

source: Most of these cancers harbor wt p53 (Soussi et al., 2005 and IRAC TP53 database, R17).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature and databases.

claim: The NGFR gene is often amplified in human breast cancers that display no p53 mutation according to TCGA genomic database analysis.
source: Analysis of the TCGA genomic database also showed that the NGFR gene is often amplified in human breast cancers that display no p53 mutation (Cerami et al., 2012; Gao et al., 2013) (Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of the TCGA database.

claim: NGFR is a transcriptional target for the p53 analog, p73, in the mouse nerve system.
source: Undoubtedly, NGFR is an authentic p53 target gene, which is also in line with a recent finding that NGFR is a transcriptional target for the p53 analog, p73, in the mouse nerve system (Niklison-Chirou et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: NGFR was originally found to be a transmembrane pan-receptor involved in the initiation, development, and maintenance of the nervous system and human cancers.
source: Our findings that NGFR can directly and indirectly suppress p53 activity were unexpected, as NGFR was originally found to be a transmembrane pan-receptor involved in the initiation, development, and maintenance of the nervous system and human cancers (Lee et al., 2001; Molloy et al., 2011; Patapoutian and Reichardt, 2001), which binds with low affinity to all mature neurotrophins, including nerve growth factor (NGF), brain-derived neutrophic factor (BDGF), neurotrophin 3 (NT-3), and neurotrophin 4/5 (NT-4/5), as well as their precursors, pro-neurotrophins, with high affinity (Barker, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: NGFR binds with low affinity to all mature neurotrophins, including nerve growth factor (NGF), brain-derived neutrophic factor (BDGF), neurotrophin 3 (NT-3), and neurotrophin 4/5 (NT-4/5).
source: Our findings that NGFR can directly and indirectly suppress p53 activity were unexpected, as NGFR was originally found to be a transmembrane pan-receptor involved in the initiation, development, and maintenance of the nervous system and human cancers (Lee et al., 2001; Molloy et al., 2011; Patapoutian and Reichardt, 2001), which binds with low affinity to all mature neurotrophins, including nerve growth factor (NGF), brain-derived neutrophic factor (BDGF), neurotrophin 3 (NT-3), and neurotrophin 4/5 (NT-4/5), as well as their precursors, pro-neurotrophins, with high affinity (Barker, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: NGFR binds with high affinity to pro-neurotrophins.
source: Our findings that NGFR can directly and indirectly suppress p53 activity were unexpected, as NGFR was originally found to be a transmembrane pan-receptor involved in the initiation, development, and maintenance of the nervous system and human cancers (Lee et al., 2001; Molloy et al., 2011; Patapoutian and Reichardt, 2001), which binds with low affinity to all mature neurotrophins, including nerve growth factor (NGF), brain-derived neutrophic factor (BDGF), neurotrophin 3 (NT-3), and neurotrophin 4/5 (NT-4/5), as well as their precursors, pro-neurotrophins, with high affinity (Barker, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: In response to neurotrophin signaling, NGFR might mediate p53-dependent neuron cell death by activating the JNK pathway.
source: Although a previous study showed that in response to neurotrophin signaling, NGFR might mediate p53-dependent neuron cell death by activating the JNK pathway (Aloyz et al., 1998), our studies as presented here unveil a novel nuclear function of this membrane receptor, i.e., to promote cancer cell proliferation and survival by directly inhibiting p53 transcriptional activity and indirectly destabilizing p53 protein via MDM2.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: NGF treatment did not appear to affect p53 level and activity in H460, HCT116, and HepG2 cancer cells.
source: These inhibitory activities of NGFR toward p53 are ligand-independent, as they occurred in the nucleus and NGF treatment did not appear to affect p53 level and activity in H460, HCT116, and HepG2 cancer cells tested (Data not shown).
evidence: This claim is stated as an observation by the authors.

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Patient derived NGFR-positive melanoma cells are remarkably capable of generating tumors, promoting metastasis, and maintaining self-renewal.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Several cancers with high NGFR expression, such as breast cancer, melanoma, osteocarcoma, and neuroblastoma, often display less or no TP53 mutations.

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: MDM2 and MDMX play a role in suppressing p53 in breast cancer, melanoma, osteosarcoma, and neuroblastoma.
source: Although MDM2 and MDMX have been shown to play a role in suppressing p53 in these cancers (Gembarska et al., 2012; Lam et al., 2010; Slack et al., 2005; Wade et al., 2013), it is highly likely that NGFR might also contribute to the reason why these cancers harbor wt p53.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: p53 has been shown to be crucial for stem cell differentiation and apoptosis.
source: Together with the aforementioned studies (Boiko et al., 2010; Tomellini et al., 2014), our findings also suggest that NGFR might play a role in maintaining the renewal and proliferating capabilities of stem cells or cancer stem cells by inactivating p53, as p53 has been shown to be crucial for stem cell differentiation and apoptosis (Krizhanovsky and Lowe, 2009) and to be a major roadblock for these stem cells to renew and proliferate (Cicalese et al., 2009; Hong et al., 2009; Kawamura et al., 2009; Marion et al., 2009; Utikal et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: p53 is a major roadblock for stem cells to renew and proliferate.
source: Together with the aforementioned studies (Boiko et al., 2010; Tomellini et al., 2014), our findings also suggest that NGFR might play a role in maintaining the renewal and proliferating capabilities of stem cells or cancer stem cells by inactivating p53, as p53 has been shown to be crucial for stem cell differentiation and apoptosis (Krizhanovsky and Lowe, 2009) and to be a major roadblock for these stem cells to renew and proliferate (Cicalese et al., 2009; Hong et al., 2009; Kawamura et al., 2009; Marion et al., 2009; Utikal et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: NGFR has been shown to exert a tumor suppressive function by repressing tumor growth in several cancers.
source: In contrast to our findings and the oncogenic role as described above, NGFR has also been shown to exert a tumor suppressive function by repressing tumor growth in several cancers (Molloy et al., 2011), which has been largely attributed to its receptor activity (Barker, 2004; Bredesen and Rabizadeh, 1997; Carter et al., 1996; El Yazidi-Belkoura et al., 2003; Khursigara et al., 2001; Nykjaer et al., 2004; Tomellini et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Pro-neurotrophin-NGFR signaling can induce neuron death through the JNK-p53 pathway.
source: One previous study showed that the pro-neurotrophin-NGFR signaling can induce neuron death through the JNK-p53 pathway (Aloyz et al., 1998), but little is known about if this is also true in cancer or if NGFR can activate p53 independent of its ligands.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: NGFR is a robust cell surface biomarker for neural crest stem cells.
source: In line with our findings, a growing body of evidence has identified NGFR as a robust cell surface biomarker not only for neural crest stem cells, but also cancer initiating or stem-like cells (Tomellini et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: NGFR is a robust cell surface biomarker for cancer initiating or stem-like cells.
source: In line with our findings, a growing body of evidence has identified NGFR as a robust cell surface biomarker not only for neural crest stem cells, but also cancer initiating or stem-like cells (Tomellini et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: NGFR inactivates p53 as a feedback regulator in cancer cells.
source: p53 activates NGFR transcription, whereas NGFR inactivates p53 by promoting its MDM2-mediated ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis and by directly binding to its central DNA binding domain and preventing its DNA-binding activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: NGFR ablation activates p53 in cancer cells.
source: Inversely, NGFR ablation activates p53, consequently inducing apoptosis, attenuating survival, and reducing clonogenic capability of cancer cells, as well as sensitizing human cancer cells to chemotherapeutic agents that induce p53 and suppressing mouse xenograft tumor growth.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.
